source_name: MNB Fizetési rendszer jelentés (Payment System Report)
why_relevant: Annual narrative report interpreting the payment statistics — gives MNB's own reading of market structure, card/instant-payment adoption and PSP competition, useful for framing and for citation-quality context.

source_name: MNB Felügyeleti hírek / hírek-újdonságok (supervisory news feed)
why_relevant: Announces new Aranykönyv releases, disclosure-rule changes and supervisory expectations — the change-detection channel that tells the pipeline when to re-fetch datasets and when a rule shifted.

source_name: MNB Engedélyezési útmutatók – pénzforgalmi és elektronikuspénz-kibocsátó intézmény
why_relevant: Licensing guidance for payment institutions and e-money issuers. Indirect but valuable: it defines the licence categories used in the register, which is how you classify HU fintech/PSP entrants correctly rather than by self-description.

source_name: MNB Speciális adatbázisok (special databases, incl. BEVA member lists)
why_relevant: Auxiliary membership and categorisation lists that cross-check the main register and expose sector groupings not visible in the institution finder.

source_name: MNB Archívum – Felügyelt intézmények (legacy PSZÁF-era pages)
why_relevant: Legacy archive of the pre-2013 supervisory site (PSZÁF heritage). Useful for historical institution lists and decisions that predate the current portal and for resolving entities that no longer exist.

source_name: Barion Payment Zrt. – Press Center / Sajtószoba
why_relevant: Barion is Hungary's first licensed e-money institution (MNB licence H-EN-I-1064/2013) and is press-release-first: milestones, merchant counts, funding (e.g. the ~EUR 6m Home Credit Group investment) and product launches appear here before anywhere else. There is no bank-style IR page, so this press centre is the primary corporate-news channel.

source_name: MNB – Számlavezető pénzforgalmi szolgáltatók és harmadik fél szolgáltatók adatai (open banking register)
why_relevant: Lists account-servicing PSPs and PSD2 third-party providers (AISP/PISP) active in Hungary, including fintechs that are not banks. Reveals which fintechs actually hold or use open-banking roles — an actor-discovery layer that the general institution register does not foreground.

source_name: MNB Statisztika – Pénzforgalmi adatok (payment statistics time series)
why_relevant: Quarterly market-wide time series on payment infrastructure, transaction volumes/values, card acceptance and payment fraud. Provides the denominator against which PSP self-reported growth claims (e.g. SimplePay's '53% growth vs 43% market') can be benchmarked, and is the only consistent source for market size when individual PSPs disclose nothing.

source_name: OTP Mobil Kft. / SimplePay corporate site and merchant documentation
why_relevant: OTP Mobil (Simple app, SimplePay gateway) is the dominant domestic online acquiring/gateway player. It publishes volume milestones (e.g. HUF 1,416bn payment traffic in 2022, +42% y/y; ~300m SimplePay transactions over a decade), plus merchant T&Cs, pricing schedules and privacy notices dated by version — a rich, timestamped disclosure trail. Also covered inside OTP Bank group communications.

source_name: B-Payment Zrt. corporate site (b-payment.com, Borgun/Rapyd-affiliated acquirer)
why_relevant: Independent Hungarian card-acquiring/PSP group; self-describes handling roughly 4 million online transactions per month. Corporate 'Rólunk'/news pages carry volume and partnership claims that are not filed anywhere else; its Zrt. accounts are separately obtainable from e-beszámoló.

source_name: PayU Hungary corporate site
why_relevant: PayU (Prosus group) is a major online payment gateway in Hungary. The local site is English-heavy and press-release-first; group-level financials appear in Prosus/Naspers reporting while the Hungarian entity files locally — a two-level disclosure pattern typical of this cell.

source_name: Revolut Bank UAB Magyarországi Fióktelepe – company record and Revolut HU announcements
source_subtype: company registry aggregator record + issuer announcements
why_relevant: Revolut completed the regulatory steps for a Hungarian branch in Oct 2025 and was entered in the MNB register as 'Revolut Bank UAB Magyarországi Fióktelepe'; in March 2026 it announced migration of Hungarian users to the local branch with domestic HUF IBANs. It reports customer milestones (2 million Hungarian retail customers reached July 2025) via press announcements rather than local IR. Branch accounts and registry data are the only structured local disclosure.

source_name: Nemzeti Cégtár / Céginfo / Cégtalálo / Companywall – Hungarian company-data aggregators
why_relevant: Aggregate and normalise filed accounts into quick financial snapshots (e.g. Barion FY2024: HUF 2.4bn net revenue, HUF 11.1bn balance sheet total, HUF 1.8bn equity, HUF 310m profit). Extremely useful for rapid triage and for spotting which PSP/EMI entities exist at all, but they are derivative and licence-restricted — the primary must always be e-beszámoló.

source_name: FinTechZone.hu – Hungarian fintech trade press
why_relevant: The densest Hungarian-language aggregator of PSP/EMI/fintech corporate news: funding rounds, licence grants, volume milestones, executive interviews (e.g. OTP Mobil strategy pieces, PastPay, SEON, Wise/TransferWise domestic-IBAN launch). Functions as both an indirect source and a strong pointer to actors that never appear in registers-first searching.

source_name: Portfolio.hu – fintech tag stream
why_relevant: Leading Hungarian business/finance outlet; tag pages (fintech, barion) give a curated stream of PSP and EMI corporate news, results commentary and regulatory decisions. High editorial quality makes it a good corroboration layer for issuer claims.

source_name: Forbes.hu – business/fintech coverage
why_relevant: Runs exclusive funding-round scoops on Hungarian payment fintechs (e.g. a EUR 10m round disclosed exclusively) and periodic landscape pieces naming the players worth tracking — a productive snowball surface for actor discovery.

source_name: Fintech.hu
why_relevant: Second Hungarian-language fintech outlet; covered the PastPay BNPL launch and similar payment-product news. Useful redundancy against FinTechZone so that a single outlet's editorial gaps do not become blind spots.

source_name: Világgazdaság (vg.hu) – payments and fintech reporting
why_relevant: Consistently first to report Revolut Hungary branch/IBAN milestones and PSP funding rounds, often quoting company statements verbatim. A practical proxy channel for issuers (Revolut, Wise) that publish no Hungarian-language IR material.

source_name: Telex.hu – economy desk (payments/licensing coverage)
why_relevant: Covers MNB licensing events for new entrants — e.g. Pay10 receiving an e-money licence and building its EU network from Budapest. Licence-grant news is the earliest signal that a new EMI will start filing Hungarian accounts.

source_name: Az én pénzem (azenpenzem.hu) – consumer-finance desk
why_relevant: Tracks new entrants to the Hungarian payment market from a consumer angle; catches smaller PSP/EMI launches that the business press ignores. Cheap breadth for the long tail of the cell.

source_name: Bankmonitor – fintech/bank market commentary
why_relevant: Analyses pricing and T&C changes at Revolut/Wise-type providers as they localise into Hungary — a proxy disclosure channel where the issuers publish only terms documents, no local press releases.

source_name: MNB licensing guidance library for payment institutions and EMIs
why_relevant: Defines the legal categories, capital and reporting obligations that determine what each actor in this cell must disclose and to whom. Essential for interpreting why one PSP files a full audited beszámoló while another (a passported branch) files almost nothing locally.

source_name: SimplePay merchant/partner document library (simplepartner.hu + simplepay.hu PDF archive)
why_relevant: Dated, versioned operational documents — financial settlement documentation, merchant guides, indicative pricing offers, data-processing notices (versions observed for 2023-11, 2024-01, 2025-03). These reveal fee structures, settlement terms and product scope changes that never appear in any press release or filing, and act as a change-detection signal for the largest Hungarian gateway.

source_name: Kosárértek.hu – Hungarian e-commerce trade portal, PSP company directory
why_relevant: E-commerce industry portal maintaining company profiles of payment providers serving Hungarian webshops. Useful for enumerating the gateway/PSP long tail (including Netpincér-adjacent and webshop-focused providers) that regulator registers list only under opaque legal names.

source_name: Vállalkozz digitálisan (MKIK) supplier directory – payment providers
why_relevant: Chamber-of-commerce accredited-supplier directory listing payment providers (Barion among them) with legal identifiers. A semi-official actor list that helps validate legal names and service categories for smaller PSPs.

source_name: GIRO Zrt. – Dokumentumok (éves jelentés, éves beszámoló, közérdekű adatok)
source_subtype: operator document repository / annual report library
why_relevant: Central document repository of the MNB-owned operator of the BKR interbank clearing system (InterGIRO1/2, GIROInstant). Holds the annual strategic report (éves jelentés, 2017-2023 observed), the audited financial statements (éves beszámoló, 2011-2025 observed), auditor reports, business reports and mandatory public-interest data (executive pay, headcount, contracts). Single richest disclosure point for instant-payment scheme economics and modernisation plans.

source_name: BKR Üzletszabályzat és Díjszabályzat (GIRO clearing rulebook and tariff schedule)
why_relevant: The rulebook and the annual tariff schedule are the only public statement of BKR/GIROInstant per-transaction pricing and participant obligations — the scheme economics that the annual report only aggregates. Versioned yearly, so a time series of tariffs is buildable.

source_name: KELER Zrt. – Pénzügyi jelentések / Éves jelentések
why_relevant: Audited annual reports and IFRS financial statements of the Hungarian CSD (central securities depository), covering settlement volumes, fee income, system investments and group structure. Directly relevant to post-trade modernisation and procurement signals.
